text: The reputation update is an asymmetric multiplicative rule in which reputation is multiplied by one plus alpha when a vote matches the revealed key and by one minus gamma when it does not, with alpha fixed at 0.05, gamma at 0.10, and a floor applied after each update.
citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Can Reputation Prevent Model Collapse? A Preregistered Test of Reputation-Weighted Data Filtering (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7598518

isBasedOn.name: Can Reputation Prevent Model Collapse? A Preregistered Test of Reputation-Weighted Data Filtering

abstract: Intelligence models increasingly learn from data that earlier Intelligence models produced, and when that loop repeats the rare cases disappear first. This paper preregisters a test of whether a reputation-weighted validator pool, filtering the training data of a recursive replacement loop, keeps those rare cases alive. The outcomes remain sealed until a replication of the original model-collapse result succeeds.

additionalProperty.name: scope_conditions
value: The parent paper requires only that gamma exceed alpha; this design fixes both rates.
Any single weight above one half is capped there and the excess redistributed among the other seated validators.

additionalProperty.name: supporting_quote
additionalProperty.value: The update is equation (3) of the RLRF paper, an asymmetric multiplicative rule. On tag t, reputation updates as ri,t ← ri,t(1 + α) when the vote matches the revealed key and ri,t ← ri,t(1 − γ) when it does not. The RLRF paper requires only (0) γ > α, and this design fixes α = 0. 05 and γ = 0. 10. Each reputation starts at ri,t = 1, and after each update the floor ri,t ≥ 0. 01 is applied.
